authority: CEO Round 159: 'Round 159 should first determine whether the response-manifold method has a mechanism-specific domain of superiority. Which failure classes are theoretically observable from dynamic response before conventional pressure thresholds, and which are fundamentally not?'
constitutional_basis: Article I — evidence precedes assertion (theoretical analysis before experiment)
Article XXXII — state strongest alternative explanation
EXPERIMENT_VALIDITY_GATE_V1 — mechanism analysis informs V2 experiment design
purpose: Before re-running C2-Y V2, analyze WHICH failure classes are theoretically observable from dynamic response before conventional pressure thresholds. This prevents a broad C2-Y kill if the method has a narrow but real domain of superiority.

obstruction.physical_mechanism: Hydraulic-resistance transition — partial or complete blockage of CSF flow path increases resistance, causing ICP to rise monotonically toward the new steady-state dictated by the obstruction.
obstruction.dynamics: MONOTONIC RISE — ICP moves from healthy baseline toward failure threshold in a smooth, monotonic trajectory. The rate of rise depends on obstruction severity.
obstruction.is_response_manifold_deviation_detectabl: NO — because the dynamics are monotonic, the response to perturbation changes GRADUALLY. By the time the response-manifold deviation is statistically significant, the ICP itself has already crossed the threshold. The manifold deviation does not LEAD the pressure; it LAGS it.
obstruction.is_conventional_threshold_sufficient: YES — a threshold alarm at 25 mmHg catches obstruction at the same time as response-manifold analysis. There is no early-warning advantage.
obstruction.theoretical_verdict: C2-Y provides NO advantage for obstruction. Conventional threshold alarm is sufficient.
obstruction.round_158_evidence: C2-Y lead time on obstruction = 0.00h (confirmed the theoretical prediction).

underdrainage.physical_mechanism: Similar to obstruction but milder — insufficient CSF drainage causes ICP to rise slowly.
underdrainage.dynamics: MONOTONIC RISE (slow) — same as obstruction but with a slower time constant.
underdrainage.is_response_manifold_deviation_detectabl: NO — same reasoning as obstruction. Monotonic dynamics do not produce early response-manifold signatures.
underdrainage.is_conventional_threshold_sufficient: YES — threshold alarm catches underdrainage when ICP crosses 25 mmHg.
underdrainage.theoretical_verdict: C2-Y provides NO advantage for underdrainage.

overdrainage.physical_mechanism: Excessive CSF drainage causes ICP to drop below normal. The dynamics involve a TRANSITION from normal to low ICP, which changes the response to posture changes (less CSF to buffer against gravity).
overdrainage.dynamics: DYNAMIC PRESSURE-RESPONSE CHANGE — overdrainage changes HOW ICP responds to perturbation (posture changes, bolus), not just the absolute level. The response becomes exaggerated (larger swings) before the absolute ICP crosses the failure threshold.
overdrainage.is_response_manifold_deviation_detectabl: YES — the response-manifold (rolling std of ICP deviation from target) INCREASES before the absolute ICP crosses 0 mmHg. The increased variability is an early signature of overdrainage.
overdrainage.is_conventional_threshold_sufficient: PARTIAL — threshold alarm at 0 mmHg catches overdrainage, but only after ICP has already dropped dangerously low. Response-manifold can detect the changing dynamics BEFORE the absolute threshold is crossed.
overdrainage.theoretical_verdict: C2-Y MAY provide advantage for overdrainage. The dynamic response change is detectable before the absolute threshold.
overdrainage.round_158_evidence: C2-Y lead time on overdrainage = 10.33h (confirmed — C2-Y detected overdrainage 10h before threshold alarm).

valve_dysfunction.physical_mechanism: Valve mechanism failure causes ICP to oscillate with growing amplitude. The dynamics are NONLINEAR — the response to perturbation changes qualitatively (from damped to oscillatory).
valve_dysfunction.dynamics: NONLINEAR RESPONSE CHANGE — the system transitions from stable (damped oscillations) to unstable (growing oscillations). This is a qualitative change in response dynamics, detectable via response-manifold analysis.
valve_dysfunction.is_response_manifold_deviation_detectabl: YES — the rolling std of ICP deviation increases as oscillation amplitude grows. This is detectable before the oscillation peaks cross the failure threshold.
valve_dysfunction.is_conventional_threshold_sufficient: NO — threshold alarm only fires when oscillation peaks cross 25 mmHg. By that time, the patient has already experienced dangerous ICP swings. Response-manifold can detect the growing instability earlier.
valve_dysfunction.theoretical_verdict: C2-Y MAY provide advantage for valve dysfunction. The nonlinear response change is detectable before absolute threshold.
valve_dysfunction.round_158_evidence: C2-Y lead time on valve dysfunction = 1.42h (partial confirmation — short lead time because oscillation amplitude grows quickly).

posture_artifact.physical_mechanism: Exaggerated posture-related ICP swings. The dynamics involve a STATE TRANSITION between supine and upright, with the transition magnitude growing as degradation progresses.
posture_artifact.dynamics: STATE TRANSITION — the ICP response to posture change becomes exaggerated. This is detectable via response-manifold analysis (large deviations during transitions).
posture_artifact.is_response_manifold_deviation_detectabl: YES — the rolling std captures the exaggerated transitions before the absolute ICP crosses the threshold.
posture_artifact.is_conventional_threshold_sufficient: PARTIAL — threshold alarm catches the peak, but only after the transition has already caused a dangerous ICP level.
posture_artifact.theoretical_verdict: C2-Y MAY provide advantage for posture artifact.
posture_artifact.round_158_evidence: C2-Y lead time on posture artifact = 9.83h (confirmed).

the_asmetry_discovered.finding: Response-manifold deviation may detect some forms of physiological degradation earlier than structural-flow failure.

class_A_monotonic_failure.explanation: Monotonic dynamics do not produce early response-manifold signatures. The manifold deviation LAGS the absolute ICP.

class_B_dynamic_response_change.dynamics: Response to perturbation changes (exaggerated swings, oscillation, state transitions)
class_B_dynamic_response_change.c2_y_advantage: POTENTIAL — response-manifold can detect changing dynamics before absolute threshold
class_B_dynamic_response_change.explanation: Dynamic response changes produce early response-manifold signatures that LEAD the absolute ICP.

the_asmetry_discovered.implication: C2-Y should NOT be promoted as a broad failure predictor. It should be NARROWED to class_B (dynamic response change) failures. If class_B provides clinically meaningful advantage, create a narrow successor (e.g., C2-Y-dynamic-response-prediction) rather than broad C2-Y.

the_question_C2_Y_V2_must_answer.question: Does C2-Y provide clinically meaningful early-warning advantage for ANY class_B failure mode (overdrainage, valve_dysfunction, posture_artifact) under a fixed false-alarm constraint?
the_question_C2_Y_V2_must_answer.if_yes: Create a NARROW SUCCESSOR targeting the specific class_B failure mode(s) where C2-Y works. Do NOT promote broad C2-Y.
the_question_C2_Y_V2_must_answer.if_no: KILL C2-Y cleanly. The response-manifold method does not provide advantage for any clinically important failure class.
the_question_C2_Y_V2_must_answer.do_not_rescue_by_inventing_new_indicatio: If C2-Y fails for all class_B modes, do NOT invent a new indication. Kill it.

round_158_results_vs_theory.alignment: Round 158 results CONFIRM the theoretical analysis:
evidence: obstruction: theory predicts NO advantage → Round 158 lead = 0.00h (CONFIRMED)
underdrainage: theory predicts NO advantage → Round 158 lead = 0.00h (CONFIRMED)
overdrainage: theory predicts POTENTIAL advantage → Round 158 lead = 10.33h (CONFIRMED)
valve_dysfunction: theory predicts POTENTIAL advantage → Round 158 lead = 1.42h (PARTIAL — short lead)
posture_artifact: theory predicts POTENTIAL advantage → Round 158 lead = 9.83h (CONFIRMED)
round_158_results_vs_theory.caveat: Round 158 results are INVALID (Article XIX violation). The alignment with theory is suggestive but not conclusive. V2 must confirm.

implications_for_C2_Y_V2_experiment_desi.reporting: Report results SEPARATELY by failure mode. Do NOT aggregate.
implications_for_C2_Y_V2_experiment_desi.scientific_kill_condition: C2-Y does not produce clinically meaningful advantage for ANY class_B failure mode → KILL
implications_for_C2_Y_V2_experiment_desi.conditional_survival: If C2-Y works for ≥1 class_B mode → create narrow successor (C2-Y-overdrainage-prediction or similar)
implications_for_C2_Y_V2_experiment_desi.aggregate_score_forbidden: Do NOT compute an aggregate score that hides class_A failure inside class_B success.
